rules.question: Does the sentence state its claim with the restrictions it holds under (assumptions, matter content, parameter ranges, limits, exceptions), in the sentence itself or earlier in its paragraph? Pass if it does, or if it makes no claim that needs one. Fail if it claims more than the restrictions stated in the paragraph allow, for example with "all", "every" or "always" where the paragraph establishes the statement for a range or a case only.
rules.source: PAPER-REVIEW, Judge every sentence, third item: assumptions, parameter ranges, limits and exceptions apply to the exact claim; design/paper-verification (user, 2026-11-25): a claim without its scope is a seeded defect

fail.tex:
\section{Conformal window of SQCD}

For $3N_c/2<N_f<3N_c$ the gauge coupling of SQCD flows to an interacting fixed point. In this range of $N_f$ the theory is an interacting conformal theory in the infrared. SQCD is therefore an interacting conformal theory in the infrared for every number of flavors.
